name: template
description: Sandboxed templating languages for boru: render text templates against a data context through one common interface, exposed as the single `Template` namespace. Four engines are implemented on the shared parse->compile->sandbox pipeline: mustache, handlebars, liquid, jinja.

conventions.import: import "./template.aql"  — the library imports its own boru:* deps (boru:parse, boru:parselang, boru:string-util, boru:vm); callers need not
conventions.call: forward, receiver LAST (canonical): `Template.render context compiled`. Piping the receiver in from the left (`compiled Template.render context`) binds identically. Group in parens to use the result as a value, e.g. `(Template.render ctx tpl)`. Receiver-first all-forward (`Template.render compiled context`) matches no signature: `boru check` reports uncalled_function and `boru X` (which checks first) does not run. Template.compile takes a single Options map, so `Template.compile {...}` and `{...} Template.compile` are equivalent.
conventions.construct: build compiled templates ONLY via Template.compile; treat Compiled fields as read-only
conventions.pipeline: each render is parse (boru:parse grammar) -> compile (to a boru program of custom tpl_* words) -> run (boru:vm sub-engine under a totally restricted policy with every capability scope uninstalled), so a template can never do I/O or escape the sandbox. On boru main the sub-engine checks and compiles that program to bytecode on every render, falling back to the interpreter only if the compile fails (see bench/BASELINE.md).
conventions.import_resolution: relative to the importing file's own directory (for `boru X` and `boru check X` alike), not the working directory; a file in test/ writes `import "../template.aql"`
conventions.errors: failures raise coded errors caught with `do [...] error [...]`. In the handler read `get "code"` / `get "message"` (a QUOTED key — `get` evaluates its key, so a bare `get code` is an undefined_word check error) or `dot code`; a bound error reads `e.code` / `e get "code"`. Codes: bad_input (compile/render args missing or wrong type), unknown_engine (engine not implemented, e.g. 'erb'), template_syntax (malformed/unbalanced template; a truly unterminated tag surfaces as parse_syntax_error from the parser).
conventions.escaping: mustache and handlebars HTML-escape {{var}} (& < > "), with {{{var}}} / {{& var}} raw; liquid and jinja output is raw by default (use the `escape` filter).
conventions.execution: boru main has one execution path: `boru X` runs a static pre-flight check, then compiles to bytecode and runs on the VM, or fails with compile_failed. --compile / --force-compile / --no-compile are retired (usage errors).

engines.liquid: {{ output | filters }} and {% tags %}: if/elsif/else/endif, unless, for/else (forloop.*), assign, comment; conditions == != < > <= >= and/or
engines.jinja: {{ output | filters }}, {% tags %}, {# comments #}: if/elif/else/endif, for/else (loop.*), set
engines.filters: liquid/jinja: upcase/upper, downcase/lower, capitalize, size/length, first, last, join, default, append, prepend, replace, escape, strip/trim
engines.not_implemented: partials/includes, template inheritance, custom helpers/filters, set-delimiters, lambdas, parent-context fallback in mustache/handlebars sections

Compiled.note: construct only via Template.compile; fields are read-only. `engine` is the engine name; `program` is the generated boru source run in the sandbox.

compile.note: Parse + compile a template once. Raises bad_input on missing/mistyped engine or source; unknown_engine for an unimplemented engine.

render.call: Template.render context compiled  |  compiled Template.render context  |  Template.render {engine, source, context}
args: context:Any, compiled:Compiled (signature order [cdata:Any c:Compiled]; receiver last)
render.note: Two forms: render a Compiled against a context (receiver LAST), or the one-shot options map (compile + render). Runs in the sandbox; raises template_syntax on a malformed template.
